project_note: The older page revision records a direct Danish path; the later page records Middle Norwegian inheritance and a Danish cognate mention. The modern comparison remains sense-sensitive.

The Danish page names Swedish vägg as a cognate. The Swedish väg page records a different root and names English way. No direct claim connecting the compared forms was found in these pages; this does not establish that they are historically unrelated.

The English entry calls ombudsman a borrowing from Swedish; the Swedish entry also records an Old Norse source and analyzes ombud + man. This supports a direct donor relation alongside the deeper source path, not a cognate-only interpretation.

The English entry records borrowing through Swedish, while the Danish entry traces ombudsmand through Old Danish to Old Norse and analyzes ombud + mand. The source records support distinct immediate paths converging on an Old Norse form; they do not prescribe one exclusive pair label.

The English entry records borrowing through Swedish; the Bokmål entry explicitly says inherited from Old Norse and analyzes ombud + -s- + mann. The source records support different paths from a shared older form.

Both entries call their forms borrowings from Swedish ombudsman. That identifies a shared donor; it does not by itself establish direct inheritance or an independent cognate relation between the English and German forms.
